title: Discrete Variance
prompt:
X takes values [-3, 3, 2] with relative weights [1, 1, 3].

Find Var(X) = E[X²] − E[X]² as an exact fraction.
hint: compute E[X²] and E[X] from the weights, then subtract the square
recap:
Variance Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²] = E[X²] − E[X]² is the mean squared deviation from the mean: the average of the squares minus the square of the average. Always ≥ 0; √Var (the standard deviation) restores the original units.

Example — [1, 2, 3] equal-weight: μ = 2, E[X²] = 14/3, Var = 14/3 − 4 = 2/3.

For a sample, dividing by n−1 (Bessel) is unbiased. Reference: Wasserman, All of Statistics, §3.
